solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feast keeps old woman in compound

indicators.note: a word that keeps something holds it within, so these letters go inside the feast word

parts.note: to feast is to dine
Pam is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A banquet that contains an elderly lady within some walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' seems to be a walled enclosure, but it is the chemical sense; 'keeps' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopamine is a chemical substance, a neurotransmitter, so it is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Where white queen starts, black causes damage

parts.note: in chess notation the white queen starts on the square d1, read as DI
sable is black in heraldry

explanation.surface: A chess game in which a black piece starts doing harm at the white queen's starting square.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 doubles as the letter I, so square d1 gives DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To disable something is to damage it so it no longer works.

clue.text: Immobilise leg

definitions.meaning: to hold them so they cannot move
... is informal slang for legs, so a ... is a leg

explanation.surface: A doctor's instruction to keep an injured limb still.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinning a wrestler holds them down immobile, and a pin is slang for a leg.

clue.text: Executive rage — animal unleashed

indicators.note: unleashed suggests letters let loose to run about freely, into a new order

explanation.surface: A boss's fury is set loose like a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Managerial describes the work of managers, so it is a fair synonym for executive as an adjective.

clue.text: Player, reluctant, eviscerated in classical drama

indicators.note: in puts the gutted letters within the classical drama word

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: eviscerated means disembowelled, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: An actor loath to perform is mangled in a classical play.
explanation.walkthrough: North is one of the four players at the bridge table; 'Player' seems to be an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge the four seats are named North, South, East and West, so North is a player.

clue.text: Flower pot almost useless

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop the pot word one letter short of its end

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware pot
US is British slang abbreviation for unserviceable, i.e. useless

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that a flowerpot is nearly no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CROCK to CROC. US, short for 'unserviceable', is British services slang for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small spring bulb with cup-shaped blooms, a type of flower.

clue.text: Extensive search through ignores luggage at first

indicators.note: ignores means the search word leaves out a letter

parts.note: to rifle through is to search hastily

indicators.note: at first takes only the initial letter of the luggage word

explanation.surface: A thorough customs search passes over the baggage at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rife means widespread, prevalent everywhere, so it is close to extensive.

clue.text: Pounds raised in Ulster — British in search for weapon

indicators.note: in places the British letter and its partner inside the search word

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly

indicators.note: raised means a letter moved up, earlier in this down entry, within the word

parts.note: taken as written: the province of Northern Ireland
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Money is collected in Northern Ireland as Britain hunts for armaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised in' moves the pounds letter to the top of the province's name, which suits a down entry; 'in' then puts that and B inside the search word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster bomb scatters many small bomblets over a wide area, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Bag male brought into class after exam

indicators.note: after means the exam word precedes the rest in the answer

parts.note: a SAT is a standard school test or exam

indicators.note: brought into means the male word goes within the class letters

parts.note: CL is the abbreviation for class
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A boy carries his bag into the classroom after a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, traditionally carried by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Fall that could lead to blindness

definitions.meaning: clouding of the eye's lens, which can cause loss of sight

explanation.surface: A tumble that might leave someone unable to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Cataract names both a great waterfall and the eye condition clouding the lens.

clue.text: This, under LA, SF and Santa A, in slippage?

indicators.note: slippage suggests the letters sliding about, a sign to rearrange them, apt for a geological fault

explanation.surface: A seismic fault lying beneath Los Angeles, San Francisco and Santa Ana, prone to slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in slippage' tells us to rearrange UNDERLASFSANTAA; the whole clue also describes the fault itself, a near &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The San Andreas Fault runs through California beneath these cities, and its plates slip against each other, so 'This' points to it.

clue.text: Violin piece by leader in strong position

parts.note: the bridge is the part of a violin that holds the strings up
a head is a leader, as of a school

explanation.surface: A violin part supplied by the orchestra leader puts them in a commanding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a fortified military foothold in enemy territory, a strong position.

clue.text: Smart but impoverished count supplanting duke

indicators.note: supplanting means one item takes the place of another, here the count word ousting the duke letter

parts.note: indigent means poor or impoverished
to tell is an old sense of to count, as in a bank teller

explanation.surface: A clever but penniless count usurps a duke's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman beside the duke, but it is the verb, giving TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligent means clever, quick-witted, a direct synonym of smart.

clue.text: Crone a non-starter in desire

indicators.note: a non-starter cannot begin, so the crone word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a witch is a crone, an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: An old hag is not a contender in the race of longing.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving, a figurative desire to do something.

clue.text: Grandfather is not such an insignificant person

definitions.text: Grandfather is not such an insignificant person

parts.words: Grandfather is not such an insignificant person
parts.note: a grandfather clock is a big timepiece, so it is not a little timer, which in hyphenated form means a nobody

explanation.surface: Grandpa is more important than he seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grandfather' is the clock, not the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-timer is an unimportant person working on a minor scale, the insignificant person of the clue.

clue.text: Key often used by news boss went in

parts.note: Enter is a key on a computer keyboard that gets frequent use
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: The newspaper editor keeps hitting one particular key on the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go in, so 'entered' is the past tense synonym 'went in'.

clue.text: Drive away from one small lake in Kansas City

indicators.note: in places the one, small and lake letters within the city name

parts.note: Dodge City is a city in Kansas, the Wild West town
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Driving off from a little lake in a Midwestern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kansas City' is not that city but a city in Kansas, Dodge City, Wild West cow town.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force something out of its place, to drive it away.

clue.text: Endless respect little man gives senior officer

indicators.note: endless means the respect word loses its final letter

parts.note: to admire is to respect
Al is a short form of a man's name such as Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A short man shows boundless esteem for a high-ranking officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a top-ranking naval commander, so a senior officer.

clue.text: Soldiers taking area in French town and city

parts.note: OR is short for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in places the area letter within the name of the French town

parts.note: Lens is a town in northern France

explanation.surface: Troops capture ground inside a French town and a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Orléans is itself in France, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Orléans is a city on the Loire in France, and New Orleans takes its name from it.

clue.text: Busy hospital in Eton failed to operate

indicators.note: in places the hospital letter inside the school name
failed suggests the school collapsing, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: to go, of a machine, is to work or operate

explanation.surface: A hospital at the famous school could not perform surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is constantly active, never resting, which is to say busy.

clue.text: Experiment involves cat finding fish

indicators.note: involves means the experiment word wraps around the cat word

parts.note: a test is an experiment
Leo, the lion, is a big cat in the zodiac

explanation.surface: A lab trial using a cat discovers a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleost is any bony fish of the large group Teleostei, which includes most familiar species.

clue.text: Greek hero puts article to varied uses

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: varied means the letters are changed around into a different order

explanation.surface: A Greek hero applies a grammatical article in assorted ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus, slayer of the Minotaur, was a legendary hero of Athens in Greek myth.

clue.text: Work found regularly in two mills

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, at regular intervals, of these words

explanation.surface: Labour is to be had steadily at a pair of factories.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil is hard, exhausting labour, a synonym for work.

clue.text: Warm house and outbuilding very good inside

indicators.note: inside puts the very good letters within the outbuilding word

parts.note: a stable is an outbuilding for horses
PI, short for pious, means very good in crosswords

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises a cosy home with a fine shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is a hospitable one: generous and friendly toward guests.

clue.text: Church under pressure to accommodate gold in hall

indicators.note: to accommodate means the church letters hold the gold word within
in a down entry under means the church part comes below the pressure letter

parts.note: or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: A church struggling to find space for gold in its meeting hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch is an entrance hall or vestibule, so in the sense of a vestibule it can be a hall.

clue.text: Light touch from one X represents

definitions.meaning: a ... in billiards or in general is a gentle brushing contact
X written at the end of a letter stands for a ...

explanation.surface: A deft touch is what a single mark stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is a gentle brush of the lips, and X stands for one in letters.

clue.text: Medicinal plant cultivated in vigneron's empire

indicators.note: cultivated suggests the soil being worked over, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A herb grown across a winemaker's estates.
explanation.walkthrough: A vigneron is a person who grows vines for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening primrose oil, taken from its seeds, is used as a herbal remedy, making it a medicinal plant.

clue.text: Rower in loud cry when losing lead

indicators.note: losing lead means the loud cry word drops its first letter

parts.note: a roar is a loud cry

explanation.surface: An oarsman roars loudly until he falls behind.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar can mean an oarsman, a person who rows, so rower fits.

clue.text: Stupid baronet plunged into river

indicators.note: plunged into means the baronet letters dive inside the river name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A foolish aristocrat has jumped into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, dull-witted, so a synonym for stupid.

clue.text: Somewhere in France that's cleaner — and very French!

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaner
très is the French word for very

explanation.surface: A spot in France where the cleaning lady is extremely French.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a French cathedral city southwest of Paris, so a place in France.
